messages:
alex_shah: Customer reporting 401 on iOS app, but response headers don't show any trace/request id. They can reproduce consistently. Endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

mia_support: Ok. For escalation we need a minimal repro bundle: timestamp (UTC), a redacted curl (or SDK request payload), SDK logs around the call, and whether there's any proxy or WAF in front of the app. Also app version and region.

alex_shah: They handed over app logs but there's no obvious request id. How do we instruct them to pull it from the mobile SDK?

kyra_eng: On mobile SDKs we usually log the request id when DEBUG logging is enabled. Quick hints:
- iOS (Swift/ObjC): open Xcode console and grep for "request_id" or "RWRequestID"; enable debug level if needed.
- Android (okhttp): look for `X-Request-Id` in network logs or enable the network interceptor to print headers.
- React Native: check the native bridge logs or call the helper `Redwood.debugLastRequestId()` if they have our wrapper.
If they still can't find it, get a curl repro instead.

mia_support: Provide them this minimal curl example and tell them to redact tokens (replace with <REDACTED_TOKEN>) before sharing: 
```bash
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 2>&1 | tee response.txt
```
This captures request/response headers and the server reply. Ask them to attach response.txt.

alex_shah: Good call. We should also ask for the exact UTC time(s) they made the request so we can correlate in our logs if the header was stripped.

jordan_oncall: If they're on a managed/private proxy, ask for the edge headers too (cf-ray / x-amzn-trace-id / x-forwarded-for). Proxies sometimes remove our request-id header. Also ask for any rate-limit or WAF logs on their side.

kyra_eng: If they can create a debug bundle, that's best. In Console: Observability -> Traces -> Create debug token (or ask support to generate one) and paste the token here. With a debug token we can pull the exact request and show the trace even if the header was missing.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: debug-token-requested by alex_shah at 2025-06-02T12:03Z — token id dbg_7f3a9 (expires in 1 hour).

mia_support: Final checklist you can paste to the customer: 1) Run the redacted curl above and attach the response.txt; 2) Attach SDK logs with DEBUG enabled (include surrounding 30s); 3) Note client clock (UTC) & app version; 4) Provide any proxy/edge headers or screenshots of network inspector; 5) If possible, generate/attach the debug token from the Console.

alex_shah: I'll send that checklist and ask them to attach the curl output and debug token. Will update thread when they reply. Thanks :thumbsup:
